We have reported multiple times on the use of Apple Vision Pro in medical settings. This week, Stryker announced the completion of the first surgery performed using an innovative application on Vision Pro.

The procedure was a hip arthroscopy using the SportSuite Vision app, which brings "critical digital content into the surgeon's virtual space." Content includes arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images.

Here's Stryker's description of the app:

SportSuite Vision brings critical digital content into the surgeon's visual space, allowing them to view physical objects in the operating room while using digital tools such as arthroscopic imaging, HipCheck, HipMap, and CT scan images. During arthroscopic procedures, surgeons often rely on multiple displays positioned at various locations throughout the operating room to access imaging and surgical data. By consolidating multiple data sources into the surgeon's field of view, this technology can reduce reliance on traditional displays and support a smoother, more ergonomic surgical workflow.

SportSuite Vision received FDA De Novo authorization on July 17. Stryker stated that the app is the first to receive FDA authorization for use with Vision Pro during surgery.

In addition, Pfizer also announced this week that it is using Apple Vision Pro to "create a memorable immersive experience" to "showcase" its commitment to "conquering cancer."

For more information about the experience, visit the Groove Jones website.
